In mathematics, a '''measurable group''' is a special type of [[group (mathematics)|group]] in the intersection between [[group theory]] and [[measure theory]]. Measurable groups are used to study [[measure  (mathematics)|measures]] is an abstract setting and are often closely related to [[topological group]]s.

== Definition ==
Let <math> (G, \circ) </math> a [[group (mathematics)|group]] with [[group law]] 
:<math> \circ : G \times G \to G </math>.
Let further <math> \mathcal G </math> be a [[σ-algebra]] of subsets of the set <math> G </math>.

The group, or more formally the triple <math>(G,\circ,\mathcal G)</math> is called a measurable group if<ref name="Kallenberg266" />
* the inversion <math> g \mapsto g^{-1} </math> is [[measurable function|measurable]] from <math> \mathcal G </math> to <math> \mathcal G </math>.
* the group law <math> (g_1, g_2) \mapsto g_1 \circ g_2 </math> is measurable from <math> \mathcal G \otimes \mathcal G </math> to <math> \mathcal G </math>
Here, <math> \mathcal A \otimes \mathcal B </math> denotes the formation of the [[product σ-algebra]] of the σ-algebras <math> \mathcal A </math> and <math> \mathcal B </math>.

== Topological groups as measurable groups ==
Every [[Second-countable space|second-countable]] topological group <math> (G, \mathcal O) </math> can be taken as a measurable group. This is done by equipping the group with the [[Borel σ-algebra]]
:<math> \mathcal B(G)= \sigma(\mathcal O) </math>,

which is the [[Generated σ-algebra (by sets)|σ-algebra generated by the topology]]. Since by definition of a topological group, the group law and the formation of the inverse element is continuous, both operations are in this case also measurable from <math> \mathcal B(G) </math> to <math> \mathcal B(G) </math> and from <math> \mathcal B(G\times G) </math> to <math> \mathcal B(G) </math>, respectively. Second countability ensures that <math> \mathcal B(G)\otimes \mathcal B(G) = \mathcal B(G\times G) </math>, and therefore the group <math> G </math> is also a measurable group.

== Related concepts ==
Measurable groups can be seen as [[measurable acting group]]s that act on themselves.
